- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price by 2–5% in 70% of cases; apply +2%–+5% bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.10–0.20 spikes, model tends to lag by 2–4 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with +1–2% adjustment.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.15+), model overfits short-term noise; smooth 3–5 day average before forecasting.
